whatIs.title: What is SBTI Personality Test?
whatIs.p1: SBTI is an entertainment-focused personality test based on 15 dimensions, featuring 30 regular questions and 2 special questions, with a total of 27 personality types. Unlike traditional MBTI, SBTI uses internet-native Chinese naming conventions, such as CTRL (Controller), BOSS (Leader), DRUNK (Drunkard), etc., which resonate more with younger generations.
whatIs.p2: The test includes hidden personality DRUNK (triggered by special questions) and fallback personality HHHH (assigned when standard personality matching is low), making the entire testing process full of fun and exploration.

f1.title: 15 Core Dimensions
f1.desc: Covering multiple aspects including self, emotion, attitude, action, and social interaction

f2.title: 27 Personality Types
f2.desc: From CTRL (Controller) to DEAD (Dead), each personality has unique characteristics

f3.title: Hidden Mechanisms
f3.desc: Includes specially triggered hidden personalities and system fallback personalities

f4.title: Visual Results
f4.desc: Each personality comes with exclusive posters and detailed interpretations

f5.title: Entertainment-Oriented
f5.desc: Uses internet meme culture and slang naming, highly memorable and easy to spread

q1.question: How long does the SBTI test take?
q1.answer: It usually takes 5-10 minutes to complete. The test contains 30 regular questions and up to 2 special questions. It's recommended to answer based on your first instinct in a quiet environment without overthinking.

q2.question: What's the difference between SBTI and MBTI?
q2.answer: MBTI is a professional personality test based on Jungian psychology theory, while SBTI is an entertainment-focused personality test. SBTI uses more down-to-earth Chinese internet language with more direct naming, focusing on entertainment and social sharing, and cannot be used as a professional psychological assessment.

q3.question: What is the hidden personality DRUNK?
q3.answer: DRUNK (Drunkard) is an easter egg personality in the test that needs to be triggered through specific alcohol-related questions. It's not one of the 25 standard personalities but a special mechanism designed by the author to present the state of 'alcohol taking over the system' in an exaggerated way.

q4.question: Why is my result HHHH (Silly Laugher)?
q4.answer: HHHH is the system's fallback personality. When your answer pattern differs significantly from the standard personality database and cannot be accurately classified, you'll be assigned this result. This indicates that your personality traits are quite unique and don't fit well with existing standard personality templates.

q5.question: Is the SBTI test result accurate?
q5.answer: SBTI is an entertainment test and does not have the rigor and accuracy of professional psychological assessments. It's more like an interesting mirror that reflects certain personality aspects in an exaggerated way. Please do not use the results for medical diagnosis, career planning, interpersonal judgment, or other serious scenarios.

q6.question: Can I retake the test?
q6.answer: Yes. However, it's recommended to wait a while before retesting, as short-term repeated testing is easily influenced by memory. Test results may vary at different times and in different moods, which is also part of the fun of personality tests.

q7.question: What are the 27 personality types?
q7.answer: Including: CTRL (Controller), ATM-er (Money Sender), Dior-s (Loser), BOSS (Leader), THAN-K (Grateful), OH-NO (Oh-No Person), GOGO (Doer), SEXY (Charmer), LOVE-R (Romantic), MUM (Mom), FAKE (Faker), OJBK (Whatever Person), MALO (Minion), JOKE-R (Joker), WOC! (OMG Person), THIN-K (Thinker), SHIT (Cynic), ZZZZ (Dead Sleeper), POOR (Poor), MONK (Monk), IMSB (Fool), SOLO (Orphan), FUCK (Fucker), DEAD (Dead), IMFW (Waste), HHHH (Silly Laugher), DRUNK (Drunkard).
